action: Confirm the receipt loss is real: reconcile S03 to S05 till receipt counts with card-terminal settlement counts and store banking from January 2025.
why: Rules out a data-capture explanation cheaply before anyone spends money on a commercial response.
kpi: Receipts per store-day vs settlement count
trigger: Any store-day where counts differ materially: report to the Data/BI Lead.

action: Collect store operating logs, staffing coverage and local-environment information (works, access, parking, events, competitor openings and promotions) for S03 to S05 and the matched control stores from June 2025.
why: Tests the internal and external explanations the Phase 6 analysis could not observe.
kpi: Share of listed data items obtained
trigger: Data not obtainable by day 30: escalate to the Head of Retail.

action: Structured area-manager visits to S03 to S05 with a fixed checklist: what changed around mid-July 2025 (access, signage, parking, neighbouring shops, competitors, hours, staffing).
why: Store teams often know about local changes that no system records.
trigger: Any identified change dated near the change point: add to the investigation log.

action: Where footfall counters with history exist, split the transaction gap since July 2025 into footfall and conversion for the cluster and the control stores. Where they do not, the past split cannot be recovered: use proxies for the past (car-park counts, public-transport or mobile-location data, card-spend data for the catchment, where obtainable) and install counters in the three stores and two control stores to measure the current state.
why: Separates 'fewer visitors' from 'fewer buyers among visitors', which point to different owners; new counters show today's position, not the cause of the July step.
trigger: Footfall gap similar to the transaction gap: external or access cause likely; conversion gap: in-store cause likely.

action: Report the weekly transaction gap between S03 to S05 and the matched control stores on the dashboard, with the change-point check re-run monthly.
why: Shows whether the loss persists, recovers or spreads while the cause is investigated.
kpi: Weekly transactions-per-store YoY gap vs matched controls
trigger: Early-warning signal EW01.

action: Hold any price, promotion or local-marketing response aimed at S03 to S05 until the investigation identifies a cause.
why: The cause is UNRESOLVED; spend aimed at a guessed cause may not work and would blur the later measurement.
trigger: Lift the hold when the day-60 decision gate names a cause.

action: Weekly zero-stock exception list for the fastest-selling Electronics & Tech SKUs on their current sales rate (last 8 weeks, new launches included), starting with the three SKUs with the largest lost-sales estimates (P00149, P00150, P00151), sent to replenishment with a named person to act on each line.
why: Full-week stock-outs are the one mechanism with root-cause evidence, and they concentrate in these SKUs.
kpi: Full-week stock-outs on listed SKUs; category availability
trigger: Early-warning signals EW03 and EW04.

action: Review reorder points and safety stock for the most affected SKUs against their current sales rate; where a parameter is out of date, adjust it as a temporary, recorded change (permanent changes wait for the I3 finding) so its effect can be measured.
why: Opening stock of the affected SKUs fell; checking the internal parameters is safe whatever the supplier's role.
kpi: Weeks of cover on listed SKUs; availability
trigger: Cover below the reorder point for two weeks on a listed SKU.

action: Request daily stock positions for Electronics & Tech so partial-week stock-outs can be measured.
why: The lost-sales estimate covers full-week stock-outs only; partial weeks are unmeasured.
kpi: Days out of stock per store-SKU (new)
trigger: n/a

issue: Voltix Distribution Ltd stock-out concentration (supply vs ordering)
action: Extract purchase orders, confirmations, ASNs and receipts for Voltix SKUs and one comparison supplier for H2 2024 and H2 2025; calculate fill rate, OTIF and lead time; compare order quantities with the ordering parameters and forecasts in force.
why: Decides whether supply or Brightwater ordering limited stock, which the current data cannot do.
trigger: Day-60 decision gate.

issue: Voltix Distribution Ltd stock-out concentration (supply vs ordering)
action: Joint fact-finding meeting with the Voltix account manager: share the stock-out pattern and ask for their delivery records and any constraint notices.
why: The supplier may hold the delivery evidence; framing it as fact-finding keeps the relationship intact.
trigger: n/a

issue: Voltix Distribution Ltd stock-out concentration (supply vs ordering)
action: No supplier penalty, delisting or re-sourcing decision for Voltix until the order and delivery review (A10) is complete.
why: The concentration is a STATISTICAL ASSOCIATION; supplier responsibility is not established.
trigger: Lift the hold at the day-60 decision gate.

action: In S13, S14, S07, S15, S16, and as a comparison sample in three stores without an increase, keep Electronics & Tech items returned as 'Faulty' for inspection (do not dispose of them or send them back unexamined) and record batch, lot or serial numbers, for an initial eight weeks.
why: Preserves the only direct evidence of whether items are defective; the comparison stores give the normal no-fault-found rate to judge against; costs little and can stop at any time.
kpi: Held units inspected; batch captured on returns
trigger: A confirmed defect in a batch still on sale: escalate to the Quality lead at once.

action: Returns-handling audit in the five stores and three comparison stores: how staff choose the return reason, and any change in guidance, systems or staff since August 2025.
why: Tests the recording-practice explanation directly.
trigger: Evidence of a coding change: restate the KPI and brief Quality.

action: Request supplier RMA and defect reports and warranty claims for the most affected products (P00149, P00151, P00214, P00205, P00146) and for all four suppliers.
why: Suppliers and warranty providers see defects across all their customers.
kpi: RMA and warranty rates by SKU (new)
trigger: n/a

action: Add batch or serial capture to the Electronics returns process in all stores (process change; a system change only if the pilot in A13 shows it is needed).
why: Without batch data the quality question cannot be answered next time either.
kpi: Share of Electronics returns with batch recorded
trigger: n/a

action: Monthly 'Faulty' returned units per 100 sold, by store and by sale month, on the dashboard.
why: Shows whether the pattern spreads, fades or follows a sale cohort.
trigger: Early-warning signal EW05.

action: Governance control: any new Home & Kitchen promotion deeper than the same SKU's depth in the equivalent prior-year promotion (or, with no prior-year equivalent, deeper than a depth band Commercial sets per mechanic) needs a written objective, a funding line and a planned post-event review on margin as well as sales.
why: The effect of deeper promotions is uncertain in sign; writing down the objective and measuring it is sensible whatever the true effect, and it cuts nothing.
kpi: Share of promotions with an objective and a review
trigger: Promotions launched without an objective: report monthly.

action: Promotion review of the H2 2025 Home & Kitchen calendar: objective, mechanic, planned vs actual depth and supplier funding for each event.
why: Establishes what the programme was meant to do before judging whether it worked.
trigger: n/a

action: Design, approve and launch the controlled test of Home & Kitchen promotion depth (see the test design), with marketing and legal sign-off and the analysis plan written before launch.
why: Only a controlled comparison can settle a question on which the four methods disagree in sign.
kpi: Test-vs-comparison-arm net revenue and gross margin per store-week
trigger: Guardrail breach in the test: stop the test arm.

action: No blanket cut and no blanket increase in Home & Kitchen promotion depth on the strength of any single Phase 6 method.
why: M1 and M4 say the programme cost revenue; M2 and M3 say it added revenue. Acting on one would be acting on a guess.
trigger: Review at the day-90 gate with the test results.

action: Weekly Home & Kitchen discount rate, promotion share and gross margin % against the approved promotion plan.
why: Detects drift in depth or frequency while the test is prepared.
kpi: Discount rate; promotion share; gross margin %
trigger: Early-warning signal EW07.

issue: Electronics & Tech range and continuing-SKU sales
action: Monthly Electronics sales split into continuing, new and delisted SKUs, with the range plan and delisting dates attached.
why: Separates normal range churn from a real decline in continuing SKUs.
trigger: Continuing-SKU sales fall while new-SKU sales do not rise.

action: Decompose the unattributed residual by store, category, product, week, price, mix, returns and availability, and check the data behind it; no operational action until a driver meets the Phase 6 evidence standard.
why: Keeps the explanation honest: the residual stays NOT ATTRIBUTED unless evidence says otherwise.
trigger: n/a

action: Start the decision log and a monthly evidence review chaired by the Data/BI Lead with the issue owners; every decision records the evidence level it relied on.
why: Makes the evidence standard part of how decisions are taken, and gives a record to learn from.
evidence_basis: Phase 8 governance; applies to every Phase 6 driver
trigger: n/a
